items.title: Trump approval hits record second-term low
items.feedTitle: Trump approval hits record second-term low: Survey
items.summary: President Trump's job approval rating has fallen to a second-term low of 37% (with 63% disapproving) in a new Economist/YouGov poll conducted after the midterm elections. The decline comes despite Republican hopes for a post-election bounce. The survey reflects growing dissatisfaction among voters following the party's widespread losses in the midterms.

items.title: Van Hollen to challenge Schumer for Senate Democratic leader
items.feedTitle: Van Hollen to challenge Schumer for Senate Democratic leader
items.summary: Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland announced he will run for Senate Majority Leader, challenging incumbent Chuck Schumer. The move comes after Democrats swept to power in the midterm elections, signaling an internal party debate over new leadership direction. The race will determine who leads Senate Democrats in the next Congress.

items.title: Wildfires threaten water supplies across U.S.
items.feedTitle: Bigger and more-frequent wildfires threaten water supplies across the U.S.
items.summary: New studies show that wildfires leave behind charred trees and scorched vegetation that contaminate streams and rivers providing drinking water to much of the country. The contamination from these fires could persist for more than a decade. The threat represents a growing challenge to water security as wildfire frequency increases.

items.title: Senators probe RFK Jr.'s Samoa trip testimony
items.feedTitle: Senators probe RFK Jr.'s reason for Samoa trip after letter refuting his testimony published
items.summary: Two Democratic senators launched an investigation into whether Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. lied to Congress about the reason for a 2019 trip to Samoa. The Associated Press and The Guardian published documents refuting his earlier testimony about the trip. The probe targets potential perjury by RFK Jr. regarding his activities during the visit.

items.title: Prostate cancer screening guidelines updated
items.feedTitle: What men need to know after a major update to prostate cancer guidelines
items.summary: The American Cancer Society issued major new guidelines recommending that middle-aged men undergo regular screening for prostate cancer, representing a significant shift in official guidance. The updated guidelines reflect evolving medical consensus on screening protocols. Healthcare providers will need to update their practices accordingly.

stlouis.title: Missouri hemp businesses close as restrictions take effect
stlouis.feedTitle: Missouri hemp businesses clear shelves, close shops as new restrictions take effect
stlouis.summary: Hemp businesses across Missouri are clearing shelves and closing shops as new state restrictions take effect. The regulatory changes are forcing operators to cease operations or significantly alter their business models. The closures represent upheaval in a sector that had recently expanded under prior rules.

stlouis.title: Ameren plans three more Missouri battery plants
stlouis.feedTitle: Ameren plans three more Missouri battery plants
stlouis.summary: Ameren is planning to build three additional battery storage facilities in Missouri as part of its energy infrastructure expansion. The plants represent the utility's investment in grid modernization and renewable energy integration. The projects signal confidence in Missouri's role in the regional power market.

stlouis.title: St. Louis school board votes to close nine schools
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis school board votes to close 9 schools - K-12 Dive
stlouis.summary: The St. Louis school board voted to close nine schools as part of cost-cutting and consolidation efforts. The closures will affect students and staff across multiple neighborhoods in the district. The decision reflects ongoing financial and enrollment challenges in the system.

items.title: Iran claims strike on U.S. radar in Bahrain
items.feedTitle: Iran says it targeted US military radar in Bahrain in retaliatory strike
items.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed it targeted and destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain in response to a U.S. airstrike on a communications tower in Sirik. The U.S. military denied the claim, saying it shot down two Iranian attack drones heading toward Bahrain instead. The exchange marks escalating tensions in the Gulf region despite ongoing U.S.-brokered talks.

items.title: Microsoft outage disrupts global services
items.feedTitle: Microsoft scrambles to fix global outage affecting Teams and Outlook
items.summary: Microsoft suffered a widespread outage affecting Teams, Outlook, and Copilot, disrupting hospitals, schools, government agencies, and businesses worldwide. The company said it was 'deeply sorry' and had addressed the underlying issue. Services began resuming over the course of the day, but the outage underscored reliance on Microsoft's cloud infrastructure.

items.title: Europe pushes for seat at Ukraine peace talks
items.feedTitle: Europe pushes for a seat at Ukraine peace talks‌ but lacks a unified voice
items.summary: European leaders are seeking participation in U.S.-brokered talks over the Ukraine conflict, but Moscow and the U.S. have not yet agreed on European representation. EU officials believe a US-led process may allow Moscow and Washington to decide the conflict's fate without European input. The debate highlights tensions over how European security concerns are addressed in negotiations.

items.title: Jaguar Land Rover reports £451m quarterly loss
items.feedTitle: Jaguar Land Rover reports £451m quarterly loss after cutting 4,000 jobs
items.summary: Jaguar Land Rover reported a £451 million quarterly loss as it counts the cost of cutting 4,000 jobs, while its chief executive called for the EU and Britain to work together amid competition from Chinese electric carmakers. The losses reflect industry-wide headwinds as automakers shift to electric vehicles. The cuts underscore ongoing challenges in the traditional automotive sector.

items.title: Nvidia scandal: Howard Lutnick faces pressure
items.feedTitle: Nvidia scandal: Howard Lutnick under pressure over alleged lack of action
items.summary: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick faces growing pressure over his apparent lack of action regarding the Nvidia spy scandal, with warnings emerging about an alleged Chinese spy's ties to Jensen Huang and delays in adding Megaspeed to trade blacklist. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has blamed Lutnick's Commerce Department for not restricting Nvidia chip exports to China. Some Trump advisers are reportedly discussing Lutnick's possible ouster.

items.title: Bus-truck collision kills at least 26 in Assam
items.feedTitle: At least 26 die in bus-truck collision in Assam’s Kaziranga; 20 others injured
items.summary: At least 26 people died in a collision between a minibus and truck in Assam's Kaziranga region, with 20 others injured. Several of the deceased were college students who have not yet been publicly identified. Prime Minister Modi announced ex-gratia compensation following the tragedy. The accident highlights ongoing road safety concerns in the region.

items.title: Delhi overtakes Lahore as world's most polluted city
items.feedTitle: Delhi overtakes Lahore as world's most polluted city as air quality drops
items.summary: Delhi has overtaken Pakistan's Lahore as the world's most polluted city as air quality has sharply deteriorated. Outdoor workers report breathing difficulties, cough, and burning eyes as the Air Quality Index worsens. The pollution crisis comes as winter weather typically exacerbates smog in the region.

items.title: India blocks 115 foreign speakers from Congress summit
items.feedTitle: Shashi Tharoor alleges 115 Bharat Summit speakers barred entry to India, their visas cancelled
items.summary: India blocked entry to over 100 foreign speakers invited to the Congress party's Bharat Summit, according to senior party leader Shashi Tharoor, who alleged their visas were cancelled. The Ministry of External Affairs responded that visa matters are sovereign. The incident raises questions about press freedom and India's openness to opposition voices.

items.title: India-Bangladesh consular dialogue postponed indefinitely
items.feedTitle: India-Bangladesh dialogue ‘at mutually convenient time’ as Hasina extradition clouds effort to reset ties
items.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs said India-Bangladesh consular talks will be held at a mutually convenient date, effectively postponing discussions. The delay comes amid spiking tensions over the proposed return of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to Bangladesh. Diplomatic sources indicate postponement reflects sensitivity around extradition politics.

items.title: Rahul Gandhi claims phone tapped by PM Modi
items.feedTitle: ‘My phone tapped by PM Modi’: Rahul Gandhi’s Instagram video and a dare
items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi posted an Instagram video alleging his phone has been tapped by PM Modi, doubling down on earlier charges and challenging the Prime Minister to a debate on the issue. The claim remains unverified and reflects ongoing political tensions between Congress and the government. Gandhi's allegations echo broader opposition concerns about surveillance.

immigration.title: DHS proposes ending deference to prior H-1B approvals
immigration.feedTitle: Removing Deference to Prior USCIS Determinations of Eligibility
immigration.summary: The Department of Homeland Security proposes to remove a rule giving deference to prior USCIS approvals when adjudicating H-1B extension petitions, meaning previously approved extensions would face fresh scrutiny. The proposed rule (not yet finalized) could affect approximately 208,000 work visa renewals and trigger thousands more requests for evidence. Comments on the proposal closed November 13, with rule publication expected afterward.

immigration.title: EAD automatic extension removed; finalized and in effect
immigration.feedTitle: Removal of Automatic Extensions for Certain Employment Authorization Documents
immigration.summary: An interim final rule published October 30, 2025, ended the automatic extension of employment authorization documents (Form I-766) for aliens who timely filed renewal applications. The change is finalized and now in effect. Workers must reapply and await approval rather than continuing to work on extended status while applications are pending.

immigration.title: State Department restricts visas linked to birth tourism
immigration.feedTitle: Protecting the Sanctity of U.S. Citizenship: A New Visa Restriction Policy for Those Who Engage in or Facilitate Birth Tourism
immigration.summary: The State Department announced a new visa restriction policy targeting those engaged in or facilitating birth tourism, revoking over 6,000 visas tied to the scheme. The finalized policy is now in effect, representing the largest mass visa revocation in U.S. history, according to officials. The measure targets individuals and facilitators of the practice, not just birth tourists themselves.

items.title: Nasdaq plunges as Nvidia turmoil deepens, Treasury yields hit 5%
items.feedTitle: Stock Market Midday, Nov. 13: Nasdaq Plunges as Nvidia Turmoil Deepens and Treasury Yields Hit 5%
items.summary: The Nasdaq fell sharply on November 13 as Nvidia's leadership crisis deepened following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, while 10-year Treasury yields approached 5%. The combination of corporate chaos at a key AI pillar and rising borrowing costs has rattled equity investors. Markets face pressure from inflation expectations and questions about AI sector sustainability.

items.title: Wholesale inflation rose to highest rate in four years
items.feedTitle: Wholesale prices rose 0.3% in October, putting annual rate at 6.5%, the highest in nearly four years
items.summary: Wholesale prices rose 0.3% in October, with the annual rate climbing to 6.5%, the highest in nearly four years. The data suggests inflationary pressures may be broadening beyond goods and into services. The hot wholesale inflation reading increases pressure on the Federal Reserve to consider rate hikes despite Treasury Secretary Bessent's concerns about a U.S.-Iran war energy shock.

items.title: U.S. home sales hit 16-year low amid mortgage rates
items.feedTitle: Home sales hit 16-year low in October amid soaring mortgage rates
items.summary: Existing home sales fell to a 16-year low of 3.75 million in October, down 8.8% from the prior year, as high mortgage rates near three-year highs and rising inflation drove buyers from the market. The decline reflects the affordability crisis gripping U.S. housing. Weak housing data may provide some offset to inflation concerns.

items.title: FIIs pour $8B into India in two weeks after exodus
items.feedTitle: FIIs and India are back together! After a prolonged break-up that saw nearly $60 billion in outflows since October 2024, foreign investors have pumped in close to $8 billion in just two weeks. Strong earnings, attractive valuations and a relative India outperform
items.summary: Foreign institutional investors have pumped nearly $8 billion into Indian markets over just two weeks after a prolonged period that saw nearly $60 billion in outflows since October 2024. The reversal is driven by strong earnings, attractive valuations, and a relative India outperformance. The flows signal renewed confidence in Indian equities after a long dry spell.

items.title: Global oil market returning to surplus as Gulf exports recover
items.feedTitle: Global Oil Market Set to Return to Surplus as Gulf Exports Recover, IEA Says
items.summary: The International Energy Agency says the global oil market is set to return to surplus as Gulf exports recover and Russian crude production rebounds, with crude at around $76–78 per barrel stabilizing. The IEA report notes that Russian production was sustained by Trump's recent diesel deal. A shift to surplus could ease price pressure on inflation and energy costs.

finance.note: Oil stabilized near $76–78 as the IEA signaled a return to global surplus amid Gulf export recovery and Russian production rebound, offering some inflation relief. U.S. stocks tumbled on November 13 as Nvidia's CEO crisis and hot wholesale inflation (6.5% annually) combined to rattle equities and lift 10-year Treasury yields near 5%. Watch: producer price data, Nvidia's interim leadership roadmap, and whether Fed rate-hike bets solidify.

cards.title: Crisis messaging under scrutiny
cards.insight: When a CEO's personal scandal intersects with national security (as with Huang and Nvidia), corporate denials ring hollow. Stakeholders—investors, employees, regulators—demand not silence but a clear, honest narrative of accountability and recovery. Evasion amplifies doubt.
cards.takeaway: In a crisis touching values (security, integrity, leadership), lead with truth and next steps; avoid deflection or minimization.

cards.title: Timing shapes perception of policy
cards.insight: When DHS proposes tightening H-1B extensions just after corporate layoffs, the optics—fairly or not—connect policy to job protection narratives that may resonate politically. The substance matters, but so does when and how the rule is announced and framed.
cards.takeaway: Coordinate messaging around major policy shifts with clear rationale; otherwise, opponents and media will fill the void with their frame.

cards.title: Silence as a political weapon
cards.insight: India's visa cancellations for opposition-aligned speakers were defended as 'sovereign' decisions, not with reasons or dialogue. This opacity itself became the story, amplifying allegations of repression more than transparency would have. Absence of explanation invites the worst interpretation.
cards.takeaway: Even when you have the authority to act unilaterally, explaining your reasoning defuses perception of abuse and shores up legitimacy.

cards.title: Momentum in markets mirrors confidence in narrative
cards.insight: Foreign investors fled Indian equities for months, then returned within weeks once earnings and valuations reset the narrative. The shift wasn't data-driven overnight; it was a collective reassessment of the 'story' of India's economy. Narrative and value are inseparable in volatile, sentiment-driven markets.
cards.takeaway: In investor relations and economic messaging, consistency and evidence-backed optimism move capital more than quarterly swings; build the long-term story.

ai.title: Anthropic IPO valued at up to $1.4 trillion
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic’s $1.4 trillion IPO valuation could reshape how U.S. investors value AI
ai.summary: Anthropic set its IPO share price range at $70 to $78, valuing the company at up to $1.4 trillion. The offering is reportedly six times oversubscribed, though the final valuation represents a pullback from earlier $2 trillion targets. Analysts are raising red flags about the company's spending trajectory and path to profitability ahead of the public debut.

ai.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for AI agent transactions
ai.feedTitle: ChatGPT’s new Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out for you
ai.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Wallet, enabling AI agents to make purchases and check out on users' behalf, starting with a limited rollout to U.S. Pro subscribers. The feature allows agents to spend money with user permission for transactions and services. The product represents OpenAI's push to integrate commerce into AI workflows.

ai.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Hydrogen, faster AI model
ai.feedTitle: Google unveils Gemini 4 Hydrogen, its new AI model built for speed
ai.summary: Google unveiled Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a new AI model built for speed that cuts hallucinations and promises faster responses in Gemini app, Search, and AI Mode. The model is designed to handle complex queries more effectively, surface relevant links, and deliver richer visual responses. The release reflects ongoing competition between major AI labs on model performance.

ai.title: Huang's exit raises questions about Nvidia's open-source commitment
ai.feedTitle: Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia’s support for open source in question
ai.summary: Jensen Huang's resignation raises questions about Nvidia's commitment to open-source AI development, including its Hugging Face acquisition and advocacy against export restrictions. The company's future support for open-weight models and open-source initiatives remains uncertain under interim leadership. Hugging Face CEO pledged to continue fighting for open-source AI despite the transition.
